rulings.decision: keep the patch observation-only (do not carry int64 through lid_header_time_buffer); fix the conversion instead
rulings.why: GROUP/STATE timestamps must record the double the sync path actually compared, because that is the quantity that decides the group boundary; substituting the raw header ns would record a value sync never saw
rulings.defect_found: llround(d*1e9) multiplies into a 256 ns grid (ULP of d*1e9 at 1.6e18) while the double spacing at 1.6e9 s is 238 ns, so 274 of 4000 adjacent double pairs collapse to the same integer ns; the floor/frac split collapses 0 of 4000
rulings.action: to_ns_exact(): sec*1e9 + llround((d-sec)*1e9); ARRIVE keeps msg->header.stamp.toNSec(); optional extra key lid_dbl=<hex bits>

runtime_library_probe.symptom: ON run FAILed at startup: 'no /proc/<pid>/maps entry for liblaser_mapping.so'
runtime_library_probe.peer_hypothesis: the check ran too early (3 s after start); move it to after the drain
runtime_library_probe.root_cause: pid resolution, not timing: liblaser_mapping.so is a DT_NEEDED entry of fastlivo_mapping (readelf -d), so ld.so maps it before main; there is no window in which the node runs without it
evidence: pgrep -f fastlivo_mapping also matches the rosrun wrapper, whose maps has no such entry
runtime_library_probe.required_fix: iterate every pgrep candidate, skip the ones without the maps entry, retry for up to 30 s, and record pid + cmdline alongside path + sha in the run dir and receipt
runtime_library_probe.why_not_move_to_end: a fail-closed check at the end turns a few-seconds abort into a wasted full drain, which is the cost just paid
runtime_library_probe.fail_closed_control: /tmp/fl_run_20261110T014109Z_2869028/receipt.json keeps path/sha null with status FAIL
runtime_library_probe.hardening_pending: pgrep -f matches the whole machine; a leftover node from an earlier SIGKILLed run has the library mapped and would be accepted with a different build's hash -- restrict to the launched process group (pgrep -g "$(ps -o pgid= -p $NODE)") or check the pid's start time
